source_text: Τάδε λέγει Σαλομὼν, ὁ τοῦ Δαβὶδ βασιλέως καὶ προφήτου παῖς ἁπάσῃ τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἐκκλησίᾳ, παρὰ πάντας ἀνθρώπους βασιλεὺς ἐντιμότατος, καὶ προφήτης σοφώτατος. Ὡς κενὰ καὶ ἀνόνητα τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων πράγματά τε καὶ σπουδάσματα, ὅσα ἀνθρώπινα. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἔχει τις εἰπεῖν ὄφελός τι τούτοις προσηρτημένον, ἅπερ ἄνθρωποι περὶ γῆν ἕρποντες, καὶ σώμασι καὶ ψυχαῖς ἐκτελέσαι σπεύδουσι, τῶν μὲν προσκαίρων ἡττημένοι, ἀνωτέρω δὲ τῶν ἄστρων τῷ γενναίῳ τῆς ψυχῆς ὄμματι, οὐδ᾽ ὁτιοῦν κατιδεῖν βουλόμενοι. Καὶ κατατρίβεται ὁ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίος ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας, καὶ ὡρῶν καὶ ἐνιαυτῶν περιόδους, ἡλίου τε δρόμους περιωρισμένους, τῶν μὲν παραγινομένων, τῶν δὲ ὑπαπαιρόντων. Ἔοικε δὲ τὸ πρᾶγμα, χειμάρρων παρόδῳ, ἀμετρήτῳ θαλάσσης ἐμπιπτόντων βυθῷ σὺν ταράχῳ πολλῷ. Καὶ τὰ μὲν δι᾽ ἀνθρώπους ὑπὸ Θεοῦ γεγονότα, μένει τὰ αὐτά, οἷον· τὸ ἀπὸ γῆς γεννᾶσθαι, τὸ εἰς γῆν ἀπιέναι, τὸ αὐτὴν ἑστάναι τὴν γῆν, τὸ τὸν ἥλιον ἅπασαν αὐτὴν ἐκπεριϊόντα, πάλιν εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν περιτρέχειν ὅρον, καὶ τὰ πνεύματα ὡσαύτως, τούς τε ποταμοὺς τοσούτους εἰς θάλασσαν ἐκδιδόντας, καὶ τοὺς ἀνέμους ἐμπίπτοντας, μὴ ἀναγκάζειν αὐτὴν ὑπερβαίνειν τὰ αὐτῆς μέτρα, μηδὲ αὐτοὺς παρανομεῖν. Καὶ τὰ μὲν ὡς εἰς τουτονὶ συντελοῦντα ἡμῖν τὸν βίον, οὕτως ἄραρε. Τὰ δ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων ἐπιτεχνώμενα ῥήματά τε καὶ πράγματα, μέτρον οὐκ ἔχει. Καὶ λόγων πολὺς μὲν ὅμιλος, ὄνησις δὲ οὐδεμία ἀπὸ τῆς πεπλανημένης φλυαρίας· ἀλλ᾽ ἄπληστόν ἐστι τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων φῦλον, πρός τε τὸ λέγειν, πρός τε τὸ ἑτέρου λέγοντος ἀκούειν· ἔτι δὲ καὶ τὸ ὄμμασιν εἰκαίοις ἕκαστα τῶν παραπιπτόντων ὁρᾶν γλίχεσθαι. Τί ἂν γένοιτο ὕστερον, ὅπερ οὐκ ἤδη τετέλεσται, ἢ πραχθείη πρὸς ἀνθρώπων; Τί καινὸν τὸ μηδέπω εἰς πεῖραν ἐλθόν, ὅτου καὶ μνησθῆναι ἄξιον; Ἐγὼ μὲν γὰρ οἶμαι οὐδέν, ὅ τι δ᾽ ἂν εἴπῃ πρόσφατον, ἢ καινὸν ἀναλογιζόμενος εὑρήσει, μηδὲ τοῖς πάλαι ἄγνωστον. Ὥσπερ δὲ τὰ πρότερα λήθῃ κέκρυπται, οὕτω καὶ τὰ ἐνεστῶτα, εἰς τοὺς μετέπειτα χρόνῳ ἀμαυρωθήσεται. Καὶ οὐκ αὐτοσχεδιάζω ταῦτα νῦν ἐκκλησιάζων· ἀλλά μοι βασιλείαν Ἑβραίων ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις πεπιστευμένῳ, ἱκανῶς ἅπαντα πεφρόντισται.
thought_title: Solomon's opening: all human affairs are empty
orientation: Solomon, son of King David, addresses the whole Church of God, declaring the emptiness of human pursuits.
pass_a_gloss: Thus says Solomon, the son of David the king and prophet, to the whole Church of God, among all men the most honored king, and the wisest prophet. How empty and useless are the affairs and pursuits of men, all that is human. For no one can say that any benefit is attached to these things, which men, creeping about the earth, and with bodies and souls hasten to accomplish, being defeated by temporal things, and not wishing to see anything at all above the stars with the noble eye of the soul. And the life of men is worn away day after day, and by periods of hours and years, and by the bounded courses of the sun, some things arriving, others departing. And the matter is like the passing of winter torrents, falling into the boundless deep of the sea with much disturbance. And the things that have come to be through men by God remain the same, such as: to be born from the earth, to go away into the earth, the earth itself to stand, the sun going around all of it, to run back again to the same boundary, and the winds likewise, and the rivers, so many, giving out into the sea, and the winds falling upon it, not to force it to go beyond its measures, nor themselves to transgress. And the things that contribute to this life of ours, so have been fixed. But the words and deeds devised by men have no measure. And of words there is a great crowd, but no benefit from the wandering idle talk; but the human race is insatiable, both in speaking, and in hearing another speaking; and still also it longs to see each of the things that fall in its way with idle eyes. What could come to be later, which has not already been accomplished, or would be done by men? What new thing is there that has not yet come to experience, of which it is even worthy to make mention? For I think nothing; but whatever one might say is recent, or new, he will find by reckoning, not even unknown to the ancients. And just as the former things are hidden by forgetfulness, so also the present things will be dimmed in time for those who come after. And I do not improvise these things now, addressing the Church; but to me, entrusted with the kingdom of the Hebrews in Jerusalem, all things have been sufficiently thought through.

pass_b_english: Thus says Solomon, son of David the king and prophet, to the whole Church of God—among all people the most honored king, and the wisest prophet. How empty and useless are all human affairs and pursuits, everything that belongs to human life. For no one can point to any benefit attached to these things that people, moving about the earth, are eager to accomplish with body and soul. They are defeated by temporal things, and they do not wish to see anything at all above the stars with the noble eye of the soul. Human life wears away day by day, through the cycles of hours and years and the fixed courses of the sun, as some things arrive and others slip away. The matter is like the passing of winter torrents that pour into the boundless deep of the sea with great turmoil. What God has established for human life remains fixed: being born from the earth, departing into the earth, the earth itself standing firm, the sun traveling around the whole earth and returning again to the same boundary, the winds likewise, and the rivers pouring into the sea—so many of them—and the winds that rush upon it, yet do not force it to overflow its limits, nor do they themselves transgress. These things that contribute to our life here have been fixed in this way. But the words and deeds devised by human beings have no measure. There is a great crowd of words, yet no benefit comes from this wandering idle talk. The human race is insatiable, both in speaking and in listening to another who speaks; and still more, it longs to gaze with idle eyes at everything that happens to come along. What could happen later that has not already been accomplished, or done by human beings? What new thing has not yet come to experience, that would be worth remembering? For I think there is nothing. Whatever someone might call recent or new, he will find upon reflection that it was not unknown even to the ancients. Just as former things are hidden in forgetfulness, so also present things will be dimmed in time for those who come after. And I am not improvising these things now as I address the Church; rather, having been entrusted with the kingdom of the Hebrews in Jerusalem, I have thought through all these things sufficiently.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'noble eye of the soul' for ὄμμα; 'careless' contradicts the noble/valiant sense of γενναῖος used earlier.
last_rejected.fix: restless eyes or wandering eyes (but note εἰκαῖος means random/vain, not careless)
last_rejected.ruling: ὄμμασιν εἰκαίοις is a different phrase from τῷ γενναίῳ τῆς ψυχῆς ὄμματι; glossary need not conflate them.

last_rejected.why: εἰκαῖος means 'random, aimless, vain' not 'careless'; the human race longs to gaze at random things with random/vain eyes.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰκαῖος can mean 'casual/random'; 'careless eyes' is within acceptable range for εἰκαίοις ὄμμασιν.

last_rejected.quote: For I think there is nothing
last_rejected.why: This is Solomon speaking (reported by Gregory), but 'I' here blurs with Gregory's own 'I' at section end; however context makes clear.
last_rejected.fix: For he thinks there is nothing
last_rejected.ruling: Context clearly identifies Solomon as speaker; no real confusion with Gregory's voice.

last_rejected.why: γεννᾶσθαι here means 'to be born' but in context of Ecclesiastes LXX it refers to human generation/birth from earth (dust); 'born from the earth' is slightly off.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ ἀπὸ γῆς γεννᾶσθαι = 'being born from the earth'; rendering is accurate and natural.

last_rejected.why: ἀπιέναι means 'to go away, depart, return'; 'departing into the earth' captures returning to dust/death.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπιέναι = 'go away/depart'; 'departing into the earth' correctly captures returning to dust.
